sn32.1:1.2: _Valāhaka_ is not explained in any dictionary I have seen. I posit a basic meaning of _vala_ as “horse”, hence _vāla_ (“horse-hair”) and with _āha_ (“day, sky”) we have _valāhaka_ the “sky-horse”, which is the name of the horse of the universal monarch ([mn129:37.2]()), and metaphorically the “clouds”. Compare Burmese *walahaka-mrang*, “flying horse, Pegasus”. Indeed, Pegasus, who was said by Hesiod to be the the bringer of thunderbolts to Zeus, may stem from the same mytheme.
